summary: Hihifo Airport (WLS) is the primary aviation gateway to Wallis Island, the larger of the two main islands in the French overseas collectivity of Wallis and Futuna in the South Pacific. Situated on the northern coast of the island, it serves as a critical link connecting this remote French territory with New Caledonia and other Pacific destinations. The airport handles the majority of travelers visiting Wallis and Futuna, a Polynesian community governed by France.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Hihifo Airport?
A: Aircalin (Air Calédonie International) is the main carrier providing regular service, typically connecting Wallis with New Caledonia and onward routes.

Q: How far is Hihifo Airport from the main town?
A: The airport is located near the village of Hihifo on the northern coast, roughly 10-15 km from Mata-Utu, the territorial capital.

Q: Are there international flights to Wallis?
A: Direct international service is limited; most international travelers connect through Nouméa (La Tontouta) in New Caledonia.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: The airport operates during scheduled flight hours only, which are limited due to the small number of weekly services.
transport_tips: Car rentals and taxis are the primary ways to reach Mata-Utu and other villages from Hihifo Airport, with the journey typically taking 15-20 minutes. There is no public bus service to the airport, so arranging transport in advance is recommended. Some accommodations on Wallis offer airport pickup services, which is worth confirming when booking.
local_tip: Flights to and from Wallis are infrequent and often weather-dependent, so build at least a one-day buffer into connecting travel plans through Nouméa to avoid being stranded.
